plan.curriculum: Mathematics 2.0, Probability, Years 5 and 6 (VC2M5P02, VC2M6P02): compare outcomes with and without equal likelihood, and recognise that the chances of all outcomes add to 1
plan.shape: problem-first: the launch game is quietly unfair, so students feel the need to compare chances before the teacher models it
plan.criticalFeature: a game is fair only when every player has the same chance; all the chances together add to 1
decisionPoints: the choice check: which game is fair?
the hinge: is the three-player spinner fair?
plan.anchor: chance = the outcomes we want out of all the equally likely outcomes
plan.catchUp: Missed earlier sessions? Write P(red) for one equal spinner with the anchor, then start at the launch.

studentTools: Printed Worksheet for every student; Extension and Supported Worksheet as needed
routineIcons: Write it, chin it, show me
boardSetup: The week's anchor on the board: chance = the outcomes we want out of all the equally likely outcomes
Under it: fair means every player has the same chance

resources.label: Worksheet
resources.description: Your turn. Decide which games are fair, find missing chances that add to 1, fix a mistake and design a fair game.
resources.title: Fair and Unfair Games
resources.subtitle: Fair means every player has the same chance. All the chances add to 1.

example.prompt: Coin: A wins on heads, B wins on tails. Fair?
steps: The chances are equal, so it is fair.

items.prompt: Write each player's chance, then decide if the game is fair.
rows: 4-colour spinner: A red, B the rest
answers: 4-colour spinner: A red, B the rest

items.prompt: Liam tossed a coin and wrote these relative frequencies. Find his mistake and explain it.
items.answer: 0.6 + 0.5 = 1.1, but heads and tails must add to 1. If heads is 0.6, tails is 0.4.

example.prompt: Make a dice game fair for 2 players.

items.prompt: Design a fair dice game for 3 players. Say which numbers win for each player, and show each player's chance.
items.answer: Each player wins on 2 numbers, for example A 1, 2; B 3, 4; C 5, 6. Each chance is 2/6 = 1/3.

items.prompt: A footy coach spins a spinner numbered 1 to 8. Jack starts on 1 to 5, Liv on 6 to 8. Which change makes it fair?
items.explain: Then each has 4 of the 8 outcomes: 4/8 each.

resources.label: Extension
resources.description: Early finisher option. Unusual dice, rock paper scissors and two-dice games, with worked examples.
resources.title: Extension: Tricky Games
resources.subtitle: List every outcome, then compare.

example.prompt: A dice has faces 1, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5. What is P(1)?

items.prompt: A dice has faces 2, 2, 2, 4, 6, 6. What is P(2)? What is P(an odd number)?
With that dice, Ana wins on a 2 and Raf wins on a 6. Is it fair? Explain.

example.prompt: How many outcomes are there when two players play rock, paper, scissors?

items.prompt: Fill in who wins: Player 1, Player 2 or draw.
Is rock, paper, scissors fair? Use the table to explain.
items.answer: Yes: each player wins 3 of the 9 outcomes, and 3 are draws.

example.prompt: Two dice: how many ways to total 7?

items.prompt: Two dice are added. Mia wins on a total of 7. Sam wins on a total of 2, 3 or 12. Is it fair? If not, change Sam's totals to make it fair.
items.answer: Not fair: Mia 6/36; Sam 4/36 (total 2: 1 way, 3: 2 ways, 12: 1 way). Fair fix: Sam wins on 2, 3, 11 or 12, which is 1 + 2 + 2 + 1 = 6/36.

resources.label: Supported Worksheet
resources.description: For students who need more guidance: spinners to count, a same-or-different check, and a hint on every question.
resources.title: Fair Games: Step by Step
resources.subtitle: Write each player's chance. Are they the same?

example.prompt: Red for Amy, blue for Ben. Fair?
steps: Amy: 2 of 4 parts. Ben: 2 of 4 parts.

items.prompt: Red for Amy, blue for Ben. Amy ___/___, Ben ___/___. Fair?
items.hint: Count the equal parts: red takes 2 of 3.

items.prompt: Red for Amy, blue for Ben. Amy ___/___, Ben ___/___. Fair?
Red came up 0.7 of the time. Not red?

slides.notes: Session 4 of our probability week: today we decide whether games of chance are fair.
Before you start, put boards, markers and a dice per pair on desks. Print the Worksheet for everyone, and a few copies of the Extension and the Supported Worksheet.

slides.title: Translate a point
prompts: (1, -2) moves 3 left and 4 up. Where does it land?

beats: SAY: Let's warm up with coordinates, percentages and graphs.
ASK: If 1, negative 2 moves 3 left and 4 up, where does it land?
25 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: (-2, 2)
SCAN boards, back row first.
80%+ -> reveal and move straight on.
Less -> do one move at a time on the four-quadrant grid. Re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: 1 take away 3 is negative 2,
and negative 2 add 4 is 2. Tick it or fix it.
trap: writing (4, 2).
Fix: ask which way left goes, and they redo the first number.
notes.prep: Review of Week 2 coordinates (the request named the focus). Keep the review under 6 minutes.

beats: ASK: What is 40 percent of 35?
20 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: 14
SCAN boards, back row first.
80%+ -> reveal and move straight on.
Less -> find 10 percent first, 3.5, then times 4. Re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: 10 percent of 35 is 3.5,
so 40 percent is 14. Tick it or fix it.
trap: writing 75 or 40.
Fix: find 10 percent first, and they multiply by 4.
notes.prep: Term 3 review: percentage of an amount.

slides.title: Read the line graph
prompts: Which day was warmest? How much warmer than Monday?

beats: ASK: Which day was warmest, and how much warmer was it than Monday?
20 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: Wednesday, 7 degrees
SCAN boards, back row first.
80%+ -> reveal, then on to Fluency.
Less -> lay a ruler across the highest point and read the scale. Re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: Wednesday was 25 degrees, 7 warmer than Monday's 18. Tick it or fix it.
trap: reading the wrong day.
Fix: trace up from each day to the line, and they read again.
notes.prep: Week 3 review: reading a line graph.

beats: SAY: Now for our seven times table.
Write each answer as fast as you can.
ASK: What is 7 times 4?
8 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: 28
SCAN boards.
80%+ -> reveal, then the next one.
Less -> double 7, then double again. Re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: It's 28. Tick it or fix it.
trap: writing 24 or 32.
Fix: double 7 to get 14, double again to get 28, and they rewrite it.
notes.prep: Times tables fluency. Keep the whole block under 5 minutes.

beats: SAY: Now a division. How many sevens make 84?
ASK: What is 84 divided by 7?
8 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: 12
SCAN boards.
80%+ -> reveal, then the next one.
Less -> 10 sevens is 70, then count on in sevens. Re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: It's 12. Tick it or fix it.
trap: writing 11.
Fix: check: 11 sevens is 77, one more is 84, and they rewrite it.
notes.prep: Brisk: one line of feedback, then the next.

beats: SAY: And a big one to finish.
ASK: What is 7 times 25?
8 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: 175
SCAN boards.
80%+ -> reveal, then the learning intention.
Less -> think of 7 lots of 25 cents. Re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: It's 175. Tick it or fix it.
trap: writing 150.
Fix: 4 twenty-fives is 100, 3 more is 75, add them, and they rewrite it.
notes.prep: Brisk: one line of feedback, then the next.

slides.learningIntention: We are learning to decide whether a game of chance is fair.
successCriteria: I can list the outcomes of a game and who wins each one.
I can decide whether a game is fair by comparing each player's chance.
I can design a fair game and explain why it is fair.

beats: POINT to the learning intention.
SAY: This week we've worked out chances and tested them.
Today we use chance to decide whether a game is fair.
SAY: Let's read our I can statements together.
Cue: Everyone, together, on three.
SAY: The first one is where we start,
and the second one is our big goal today.
notes.prep: SC1 listing outcomes is reachable for everyone; SC2 comparing chances is the core and the exit evidence; SC3 designing a fair game is the stretch.

slides.title: Would you play this game?
lines: Player A wins on 1 or 2. Player B wins on 3, 4, 5 or 6.

notes.answer: not fair: B has 4/6, A has 2/6
beats: POINT to the rules.
SAY: Here's a dice game for two players. Read the rules with me.
ASK: Is this game fair? Thumbs up for fair, down for not fair.
10 sec. Cue: Thumbs only, voices off. Show me... now.
EXPECT: thumbs down
ASK: Tell your partner which player you would rather be, and why.
20 sec. Cue: Partner A first. You have 20 seconds. Go.
EXPECT: B: four numbers win, A only has two
SAY: B wins on 4 of the 6 outcomes, but A only wins on 2.
So it isn't fair. Today we learn to check any game, exactly.
trap: saying fair because there are two players.
Fix: count the winning numbers for each player, and they decide again.
notes.prep: Problem-first: the unfair game shows the need to compare chances. Under 4 minutes.

slides.meaning: Every player has the same chance of winning.
slides.example: Heads for me, tails for you is fair: 1/2 each.

notes.answer: every player has the same chance
beats: POINT to the word.
SAY: In maths, fair has an exact meaning. Say it with me: fair.
SAY: A game is fair when every player has the same chance of winning.
The scales balance.
ASK: Is 'heads for me, tails for you' fair? Thumbs up or down.
5 sec. Cue: Thumbs only, voices off. Show me... now.
EXPECT: thumbs up
trap: thinking fair means everyone wins sometimes.
Fix: compare the two chances, and they check again.
notes.prep: Fair means equal chances, not 'it feels fine'.

slides.title: Is the game fair?
steps: Equal chances, so it is fair.

visual.text: Dice game: A wins on an even number. B wins on an odd number.

beats: MODEL listing the outcomes.
SAY: To check a game, I list every outcome first:
MODEL sorting them by winner.
SAY: A wins on the even numbers, 2, 4 and 6.
B wins on 1, 3 and 5.
That's 3 out of 6 each.
ASK: Is this game fair? Write yes or no, and each chance.
15 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: yes, 3/6 each
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: Yes, it's fair: 3 sixths each.
Same chance, fair game.
trap: judging by how many players there are.
Fix: list the outcomes for each player, and they compare.
notes.stretch: Change one rule to make it unfair for B.
notes.help: Write A or B under each number from 1 to 6.
notes.prep: List, sort, compare: the routine for any game. SC1 and SC2.

beats: POINT to each colour.
SAY: Red is 3 of 6 equal parts, blue is 1, and green is 2.
MODEL adding the chances.
SAY: When I add all the chances, I get 6 sixths, which is 1.
Something has to happen, so all the chances together are certain.
ASK: The same is true for results. Red came up 0.45 and blue 0.3.
What was green?
20 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: 0.25
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: 0.45 and 0.3 make 0.75, so green is 0.25.
Everything adds to 1.
trap: adding to 100 with decimals.
Fix: say decimals add to 1, and they redo it.
notes.stretch: Write a spinner where the chances are 1/2, 1/3 and 1/6.
notes.help: Count the equal parts and check they make the whole.
notes.prep: Chances and relative frequencies add to 1. SC2.

slides.title: Which game is fair?
slides.prompt: Point to A, B or C

options.text: Spinner, half red, half blue. Red wins for Amy, blue for Ben.
Dice. Amy wins on 1 to 4, Ben on 5 or 6.
options.misconception: thinks two players means 50/50, without counting outcomes

options.text: Equal spinner: red, blue, green. Amy wins red, Ben wins blue or green.
options.misconception: only checks that each player has a colour

beats: SAY: Work out each player's chance before you choose.
ASK: Which game is fair?
20 sec. Cue: Voices off. Point... now. Hold your point.
EXPECT: pointing to A
SCAN the room, back row first.
80%+ -> reveal, then cold call one student: Ben's chance in B?
Less -> write each player's chance for B and C on the board. Re-ask.
REVEAL after pointing is scanned.
SAY: It's A: one half each. In B, Amy has 4/6 and Ben 2/6.
In C, Ben has 2/3 and Amy only 1/3.
trap: pointing to B.
Fix: list who wins on each dice number, and they choose again.
notes.prep: First decision point. B: two players assumed to be 50/50; C: one colour each assumed to be fair.

slides.title: Fair or unfair?
slides.ask: Is it fair? Write F or U, and each player's chance.
slides.pivot: list the outcomes and write the winner under each one
slides.followUp: cold call one board: How did you compare?

items.text: Dice: Mia wins on 6, Sam wins on 1.
items.say: Fair: 1/6 each, even though most rolls nobody wins.

items.text: Dice: Mia wins on 2, 3 or 5. Sam on 1, 4 or 6.
Two coins: Mia wins on two heads, Sam on one of each.
items.say: Unfair: HT and TH both win for Sam, so 2/4 against 1/4.

say: Write F or U, and each chance, on your board.
trap: calling a game unfair when nobody wins some outcomes.
Fix: compare only the players' chances, and they decide again.
notes.stretch: Fix each unfair game in the smallest way.
notes.help: Write the winner under each outcome first.
notes.prep: Guided practice, including fair with non-winning outcomes and a two-coin game. SC2.

beats: SAY: This one is just for you.
Each person wins on their own part of the spinner.
ASK: Is this three-player game fair? Write yes or no, and Cal's chance.
25 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: no, Cal 2/8
SCAN every board, back row first.
80%+ -> reveal, then Your turn.
Less -> split the spinner into 8 equal parts and count each name. Re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: Not fair. Amy and Ben have 3 eighths, but Cal only has 2.
Tick it or fix it.
trap: saying fair because each has a part.
Fix: split into equal parts and count, and they decide again.
notes.prep: The hinge before independent work. Anyone saying fair starts on the Supported Worksheet with the teacher.

slides.title: Your turn
slides.task: Decide which games are fair and design your own on your worksheet.

beats: POINT to the steps.
SAY: Read each question carefully, solve it carefully, then check your answers.
SAY: If you finish, the Extension is your early finisher option.
Let's read the steps together. Cue: Everyone, together, on three.
CIRCULATE and ask: What is each player's chance?
TIME: 20 minutes. Stop everyone once at 10 minutes to share a strategy.
trap: judging a game without counting outcomes.
Fix: list the outcomes and winners, and they redo it.
notes.stretch: Extension: unusual dice, rock paper scissors and a two-dice game.
notes.help: Supported Worksheet: spinners to count, a same-or-different check and hints.
notes.prep: Independent practice: fair or not, chances adding to 1, a mistake and designing a fair game. The sheet is evidence for SC2 and SC3.

slides.title: Show what you know
questions: Is this dice game fair? Give each player's chance.

visual.text: Jo wins on 1, 2 or 3. Pat wins on 4 or 5. A 6 means roll again.

beats: SAY: Here's the last one. Work it out on your own board.
ASK: Is this dice game fair? Give each player's chance.
30 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: not fair: Jo 3/6, Pat 2/6
RECORD who calls it fair or cannot give the chances.
Their names go to next week's catch-up group.
trap: saying fair.
Fix: none now. Record the name for tomorrow.
notes.prep: Exit evidence for SC2 across the week: compare two chances in a new game.

slides.reflectionPrompt: Tell your partner how to check whether a game is fair.

notes.answer: open - listen for list the outcomes and compare each player's chance
beats: SAY: Let's read our I can statements together.
Cue: Everyone, together, on three.
ASK: How sure are you that you can decide whether a game is fair?
5 sec. Cue: Thumbs only, voices off. Show me... now.
EXPECT: thumbs up, sideways or down
RECORD each thumb down beside the exit board.
A thumb up with 'fair' on the exit board matters most.
ASK: How do you check whether a game is fair?
20 sec. Cue: Partner B first. You have 20 seconds. Go.
EXPECT: list the outcomes and compare each player's chance
notes.prep: Week close: read the self-assessment beside the exit evidence for next week's review.
